content: 1. Dosing for dicloxacillin in severe infections is 50-100 mg/kg/day orally, divided into doses every 6 hours. For patients weighing ≥40 kg, the dose is 125-500 mg orally every 6 hours. It should be taken on an empty stomach. 2. Dicloxacillin decreases the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. 3. Dicloxacillin and the cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 4. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Doxycycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Dicloxacillin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may decrease efficacy if coadministered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 7. Minocycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Omadacycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 10. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Sarecycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Dicloxacillin decreases the efficacy of the typhoid live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. 13. Dicloxacillin and aspirin may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Dicloxacillin and aspirin (rectal) may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Dicloxacillin and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of atezolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 17. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose adjustment is recommended when used with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 18. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of avelumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 19. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels of axitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Azithromycin reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Aztreonam and dicloxacillin may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination may be used synergistically against Enterobacteriaceae. 22. Chloramphenicol reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Colestipol decreases the levels of dicloxacillin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Nitazoxanide and dicloxacillin may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine (antidote) by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Probenecid increases the levels of dicloxacillin by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 29. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 30. Dicloxacillin and parecoxib may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 31. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 32. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 33. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels of phenindione by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Dicloxacillin and piroxicam may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 35. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 36. Dicloxacillin and salicylates (non-ASA) may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor. 37. Dicloxacillin and salsalate may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 38. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 39. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor. 40. Dicloxacillin and sulfasalazine may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 41. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 44. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 45. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dose adjustment is recommended with concomitant use of ubrogepant and moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 46. Dicloxacillin and willow bark may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. 47. Dicloxacillin increases the levels of methotrexate by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. Increased serum concentrations of methotrexate with concurrent hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity have been observed with concurrent administration of high or low doses of methotrexate and penicillins. 48. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels of mycophenolate by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. This may reduce concentrations of the active metabolite of mycophenolate, possibly by impairing enterohepatic circulation. 49. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 50. Dicloxacillin decreases the effects of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 51. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 52. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinylestradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 53. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor.
